categories.main_business_segments: Wingstop operates in a single business segment focused on franchising and operating fast casual chicken wing restaurants. The company’s system consists of both franchised and company-owned restaurants, with approximately 98% of locations franchised as of December 28, 2024.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Wingstop’s core production method centers on preparing fresh, cooked-to-order chicken wings, tenders, and sandwiches, hand-sauced in proprietary flavors. The company leverages a proprietary digital ordering platform, integrated POS systems, and a streamlined supply chain with designated suppliers and a single national distributor for U.S. operations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are individual consumers seeking fast casual dining, with a focus on chicken wings, tenders, and sandwiches. Key end markets include dine-in, carryout, and delivery, serving both individual and group occasions, with a strong emphasis on digital ordering and delivery channels.
categories.geographic_coverage: Wingstop operates over 2,550 restaurants in 45 U.S. states and 12 countries and U.S. territories, with 359 international locations as of December 28, 2024. The largest domestic markets are Texas, California, Florida, and Illinois, and the company is actively expanding both domestically and internationally.
categories.supply_chain_position: Wingstop is positioned downstream in the supply chain as a restaurant operator and franchisor. The company manages relationships with approved suppliers and a national distributor, ensuring quality and consistency across its franchised and company-owned restaurants.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include sustaining long-term same store sales growth through brand awareness, menu innovation, digital leadership, and data-driven marketing. The company is investing in technology, expanding its global footprint, and maintaining best-in-class unit economics, with ongoing enhancements to its proprietary digital platform and supply chain.
categories.revenue_model: Wingstop generates revenue primarily through royalties, advertising fees, and franchise fees from franchisees, as well as sales from company-owned restaurants. The asset-light, highly-franchised model emphasizes recurring royalty and fee income, supplemented by direct restaurant sales.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Wingstop competes in the intensely competitive fast casual and quick service restaurant industry, facing national and regional chains offering chicken wings, tenders, and sandwiches, as well as other foodservice and delivery providers. The company is the largest fast casual chicken wing-focused chain globally and emphasizes its digital and flavor leadership.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of fiscal year 2024, Wingstop reported $625.8 million in total revenue (up 36% year-over-year), $4.8 billion in system-wide sales, and net income of $108.7 million (up 54.9%). The company opened 349 net new restaurants in 2024, achieving 19.9% domestic same store sales growth and maintaining a strong, capital-efficient growth trajectory.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Wingstop differentiates itself through bold, distinctive flavors, fresh cooked-to-order menu items, and a highly customizable guest experience. The brand emphasizes operational simplicity, digital ordering leadership (with over 70% digital sales domestically), and attractive unit economics for franchisees, driving repeat business and strong brand loyalty.
